precepts.why:
“So shall the king of Assyria lead away the Egyptians prisoners, and the Ethiopians captives, young and old, naked and barefoot, even with their buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.”

The scholars read the cruel lord of Isaiah 19:4 as one of the kings of Assyria that smote Egypt after the time of Isaiah, and that is what Isaiah goes into here. But the scriptures have dual meanings: what was done to ancient Egypt is what we see happening to spiritual Egypt now.

moments.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?
GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon the king of Assyria, and fought against Ashdod and took it, the Most High spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz.

note.label: Isaiah 20: Naked and Barefoot for a Sign

points: He told Isaiah to loose the sackcloth from his loins and put off his shoe from his foot, and Isaiah did so, walking naked and barefoot.

note.label: Isaiah 20: Naked and Barefoot for a Sign

points: As Isaiah walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and wonder upon Egypt and Ethiopia, so the king of Assyria would lead the Egyptians and Ethiopians away captive, young and old, naked and barefoot, even with their buttocks uncovered to the shame of Egypt.
Having the buttocks uncovered is a shame; young brothers should stop all that sagging, since the scripture itself marks an uncovered backside as a disgrace.

note.label: Isaiah 20: Naked and Barefoot for a Sign

points: The inhabitants of the isle shall say in that day that such is their expectation, ashamed and afraid, and ask how they shall escape the king of Assyria.

note.label: Isaiah 20: Naked and Barefoot for a Sign

points: Shalmaneser dies, and his relative, some say his brother, some say a cousin, takes over after him and does the same thing. “In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,) and fought against Ashdod, and took it”. Tartan was Sargon’s captain or commander.

Sargon reigned right after Shalmaneser, of the same royal family, and historically he finished what Shalmaneser did not complete. He was the last wave of removing the northern kingdom out of the land and placing them in the Assyrian areas, the cities of the Medes, around 722, 721 BC. Shalmaneser and Sargon were around the same time frame, one a little after the other, and one finished the other’s job of deporting our people into foreign lands.
Out of Sargon came the king who attacked Judah, and the angel came and killed all his men, 185,000 of them to be exact.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: “In the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod, (when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him,)”. Tartan was a general of Sargon. Sargon was of the same royal line as Shalmaneser (some say brother, some say cousin), and Sargon was the final blow against the northern kingdom: he completed what Shalmaneser left off.

Pul, Tiglath-pileser, came first and took a wave of us away. Then Shalmaneser came and took the bulk, the majority of us, and Sargon took away the remainder of that bulk. But there was a remnant left.
